49913-nine-unlikely-tales.title: Nine Unlikely Tales
49913-nine-unlikely-tales.creator: Unknown
49913-nine-unlikely-tales.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. MATILDA’S ears were red and shiny. This was because Pridmore had washed her. It was not the usual washing, which makes you clean and comfortable, but the “thorough good wash,” which makes you burn and smart till you wish you could be like the poor little savages who do not know anything, and run about bare in the sun, and only go into the water when they are hot.

arxiv-2001-01924.title: A semi-supervised learning framework for quantitative structure-activity regression modelling
arxiv-2001-01924.creator: Oliver Watson 1,∗ , Isidro Cortes-Ciriano 2 , James A Watson 3,4
arxiv-2001-01924.description: Abstract Supervised learning models, also known as quantitative structure-activity regression (QSAR) models, are increasingly used in assisting the process of preclinical, small molecule drug discovery. The models are trained on data consisting of a finite dimensional representation of molecular structures and their corresponding target specific activities.

arxiv-2103-02126.title: Differentiable Neural Architecture Learning for Efficient Neural Network Design Manuscript received June 28, 2019
arxiv-2103-02126.creator: Qingbei Guo 1 2 , Xiao-Jun Wu 1 , Josef Kittler 3 , , Zhiquan Feng 2
arxiv-2103-02126.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Qingbei Guo 1 2 , Xiao-Jun Wu 1 , Josef Kittler 3 , , Zhiquan Feng 2. Automated neural network design has received ever-increasing attention with the evolution of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs), especially involving their deployment on embedded and mobile platforms. One of the biggest problems that neural architecture search (NAS) confronts is that a large number of candidate neural architectures are required to train, using, for instance, reinforcement learning and evolutionary optimisation algorithms, at a vast computation cost.

Both authors were partially supported by the Germ
arxiv-2112-00430.creator: Juan Pablo Acosta López, Martin Hils
arxiv-2112-00430.description: Abstract . We give a complete list of the commutative one-dimensional groups definable in algebraically closed valued fields and in pseudo-local fields, up to a finite index subgroup and quotienting by a finite subgroup. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 03C60, Secondary: 03C98, 11G07, 11U09, 12J25. 1.

arxiv-2301-06423.title: On a generalization of the spectral Mantel’s theorem
arxiv-2301-06423.creator: Chunmeng Liu, Changjiang Bu
arxiv-2301-06423.description: Abstract Mantel’s theorem is a classical result in extremal graph theory which implies that the maximum number of edges of a triangle-free graph of order n n . In 1970, E. Nosal obtained a spectral version of Mantel’s theorem which gave the maximum spectral radius of a triangle-free graph of order n n .

arxiv-2302-11680.title: Hilbert space fragmentation in a long-range system
arxiv-2302-11680.creator: Gianluca Francica, Luca Dell’Anna
arxiv-2302-11680.description: Abstract We study the role of the interaction range on the Hilbert-space fragmentation and many-body scar states considering a spin-1/2 many-body Hamiltonian describing a generalized Fredkin spin chain. We show that both scar states and weak fragmentation of the Hilbert space survive for almost any range of the coupling.

This mat
arxiv-2303-16114.creator: David Loeffler, Óscar Rivero
arxiv-2303-16114.description: Abstract . We prove algebraicity results for critical L L -values attached to the group GSp 4 × GL 2 \GSp_{4}\times\GL_{2} , and for Gan–Gross–Prasad periods which are conjecturally related to central L L -values for GSp 4 × GL 2 × GL 2 \GSp_{4}\times\GL_{2}\times\GL_{2} .

arxiv-2307-04287.title: Generalizing Graph ODE for Learning Complex System Dynamics across Environments Conference: Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 6–10, 2023; Long Beach, CA, USA Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Minin
arxiv-2307-04287.creator: Zijie Huang, Yizhou Sun, Wei Wang
arxiv-2307-04287.description: Abstract . Learning multi-agent system dynamics has been extensively studied for various real-world applications, such as molecular dynamics in biology, multi-body system in physics, and particle dynamics in material science. Most of the existing models are built to learn single system dynamics, which learn the dynamics from observed historical data and predict the future trajectory.

arxiv-2406-08641.title: ML-SUPERB 2.0: Benchmarking Multilingual Speech Models Across Modeling Constraints, Languages, and Datasets Thanks: * Equal contribution.
arxiv-2406-08641.creator: Jiatong Shi, Shih-Heng Wang, William Chen, Martijn Bartelds, Vanya Bannihatti Kumar, Jinchuan Tian, Xuankai Chang, Dan Jurafsky, Karen Livescu, Hung-yi Lee, Shinji Watanabe
arxiv-2406-08641.description: Abstract ML-SUPERB evaluates self-supervised learning (SSL) models on the tasks of language identification and automatic speech recognition (ASR). This benchmark treats the models as feature extractors and uses a single shallow downstream model, which can be fine-tuned for a downstream task. However, real-world use cases may require different configurations. This paper presents ML-SUPERB 2.

arxiv-2409-01991.title: Temporal Evolution of the Radial Distribution of Milky Way Satellite Galaxies
arxiv-2409-01991.creator: Ekta Patel, Lipika Chatur, Yao-Yuan Mao
arxiv-2409-01991.description: Abstract The Milky Way (MW) is surrounded by dozens of satellite galaxies, with six-dimensional (6D) phase space information measured for over 80% of this population. The spatial distribution of these satellites is an essential probe of galaxy formation and for mapping the MW’s underlying dark matter distribution.

arxiv-2412-16667.title: The Good, the Bad, and the (Un)Usable: A Rapid Literature Review on Privacy as Code
arxiv-2412-16667.creator: Nicolás E. Díaz Ferreyra 1 , Sirine Khelifi 1 , Nalin Arachchilage 2 and Riccardo Scandariato 1
arxiv-2412-16667.description: Abstract Privacy and security are central to the design of information systems endowed with sound data protection and cyber resilience capabilities. Still, developers often struggle to incorporate these properties into software projects as they either lack proper cybersecurity training or do not consider them a priority.

arxiv-2505-22391.title: Physics-Informed Distillation of Diffusion Models for PDE-Constrained Generation
arxiv-2505-22391.creator: Yi Zhang, Peng Wang, Difan Zou
arxiv-2505-22391.description: Abstract Diffusion models show growing promise for generative modeling of physical systems, but enforcing partial differential equation (PDE) constraints directly is infeasible during the stochastic denoising process. Current methods apply constraints to the expected clean sample, incurring a Jensen’s Gap that forces a trade-off between PDE satisfaction and generative accuracy.

arxiv-2506-18285.title: Learning Causal Graphs at Scale: A Foundation Model Approach
arxiv-2506-18285.creator: Naiyu Yin, Tian Gao, Yue Yu
arxiv-2506-18285.description: Abstract Due to its human-interpretability and invariance properties, Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) has been a foundational tool across various areas of AI research, leading to significant advancements. However, DAG learning remains highly challenging, due to its super-exponential growth in computational cost and identifiability issues, particularly in small-sample regimes.

arxiv-2602-11274.title: Evolution of the transitional millisecond pulsar PSR J1023+0038 from Aqueye+ and NICER observations
arxiv-2602-11274.creator: S. Conforti ,, L. Zampieri, M. Fiori, A. Spolon, G. Naletto, A. Burtovoi
arxiv-2602-11274.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by S. Conforti ,, L. Zampieri, M. Fiori, A. Spolon, G. Naletto, A. Burtovoi. Transitional Millisecond Pulsars (tMSPs) are old, rapidly rotating neutron stars spun up by accretion from a low-mass companion star. These objects can switch between two emission regimes: rotation-powered radio pulsar and accreting X-ray pulsar.

arxiv-2602-17526.title: The Anxiety of Influence: Bloom Filters in Transformer Attention Heads
arxiv-2602-17526.creator: Peter Balogh
arxiv-2602-17526.description: Abstract Some transformer attention heads appear to function as membership testers—dedicating themselves to answering the question “has this token appeared before in the context?” We identify these heads across four language models (GPT-2 small, medium, and large; Pythia-160M) and show that they form a spectrum of membership-testing strategies.

arxiv-2604-19481.title: Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing with Trapped Ions: The Walking Cat Architecture
arxiv-2604-19481.creator: Felix Tripier, Woo Chang Chung, Jacob Young, Safwan Alam, Bryce Bjork, Aharon Brodutch, Finn Lasse Buessen, Nolan J. Coble, Thomas Dellaert, Dmitri Maslov, Martin Roetteler, Edwin Tham, Mark Webster, Min Ye, John Gamble, Andrii Maksymov, J. P. Marceaux, Nicolas Delfosse

arxiv-2606-00917.creator: André L. F. de Almeida, George C. Alexandropoulos

pmc-10736957.title: A TWO-YEAR RCT EXAMINING SPEED OF PROCESSING TRAINING ON EVERYDAY FUNCTIONING IN ADULTS WITH HAND IN THE US DEEP SOUTH
pmc-10736957.creator: David Vance, Pariya Fazeli, Andres Azuero, Sarah Khalidi, Jennifer Frank, Virgina Wadely, James Raper, Caitlin Pope
pmc-10736957.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Approximately 44% of people living with HIV (PLWH) experience HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND). Cognitive training approaches, such as speed of processing (SOP) training, may reduce the detrimental impact of HAND on everyday functioning.

pmc-11311029.title: The Royal Zoological Society of Scotland’s Approach to Assessing and Promoting Animal Welfare in Collaboration with Universities
pmc-11311029.creator: Kristine M. Gandia, Jo Elliott, Simon Girling, Sharon E. Kessler, Hannah M. Buchanan-Smith
pmc-11311029.description: Simple SummaryAll good zoos have animal welfare assessment policies and practices in place to promote their animals’ welfare, 24/7, across the lifespan. Here, we describe the approaches that The Royal Zoological Society of Scotland’s (RZSS) Edinburgh Zoo and Highland Wildlife Park take to providing conditions for animals to thrive in captivity, in collaboration with universities.

pmc-11377292.title: JAK inhibitors to treat STAT3 gain-of-function: a single-center report and literature review
pmc-11377292.creator: Faranaz Atschekzei, Stephan Traidl, Julia Carlens, Katharina Schütz, Sandra von Hardenberg, Abdulwahab Elsayed, Diana Ernst, Linus Risser, Thea Thiele, Theresa Graalmann, Juliana Raab, Ulrich Baumann, Torsten Witte, Georgios Sogkas
pmc-11377292.description: ObjectiveThe signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) gain-of-function (GOF) syndrome (STAT3-GOF) is an inborn error of immunity (IEI) characterized by diverse manifestations of immune dysregulation that necessitate systemic immunomodulatory treatment. The blockade of the interleukin-6 receptor and/or the inhibition of the Janus kinases has been commonly employed to treat diverse STAT3-GOF-associated manifestations.

pmc-11430212.title: Recent Developments in Personal Glucose Meters as Point-of-Care Testing Devices (2020–2024)
pmc-11430212.creator: Dan-Ni Yang, Shan Geng, Rong Jing, Hao Zhang
pmc-11430212.description: Point-of-care testing (POCT) is a contemporary diagnostic approach characterized by its user-friendly nature, cost efficiency, environmental compatibility, and lack of reliance on professional experts. Therefore, it is widely used in clinical diagnosis and other analytical testing fields to meet the demand for rapid and convenient testing.

pmc-11622222.title: Combined Quantification and Characterization of Dissolved Organic Matter by Liquid Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry Using Charged Aerosol Detection
pmc-11622222.creator: Stacey
pmc-11622222.description: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is a complex mixture of thousands of molecular formulas comprised of an unknown number of chemical compounds, the concentration and composition of which are critical to ecosystem function and biogeochemical cycling. Despite its importance, our understanding of the DOM composition is lacking.

pmc-11671697.title: The Australian Frailty Network: Development of a consumer‐focussed national response to frailty
pmc-11671697.creator: Natasha Reid, Adrienne Young, Loretta Baldassar, Anja Christoffersen, Tracy Comans, Simon Conroy, Christopher Etherton‐Beer, Jason Ferris, Maria Fiatarone Singh, Sarah Fox, Emily H. Gordon, Manonita Ghosh, Chandana Guha, Sarah Hilmer, Lisa Kouladjian O’Donnell, Benignus Logan, Kristiana Ludlow, Mich
pmc-11671697.description: Frailty is an important concept in the care of older adults. Over the past two decades, significant advances have been made in measuring frailty. While it is now well‐recognised that frailty status is an important determinant of outcomes from medical illnesses or surgical interventions, frailty measurement is not currently routinely integrated into clinical practice.

pmc-12524622.title: Macrophage Migration Inhibitory Factor and Post-Discharge Inflammatory Profiles in Severe COVID-19: A Prospective Observational Study from Romania
pmc-12524622.creator: Nimród László, Corina Mărginean, Botond Barna Mátyás, Cristina Alexandra Man, Előd Ernő Nagy, Gabriela Jimborean, Jacek Z Kubiak, Theodoros Karampitsakos, Brenda M Juan-Guardela
pmc-12524622.description: Dysregulated cytokine responses are a hallmark of severe COVID-19; however, the persistence of these responses following hospital discharge remains inadequately understood. This study aimed to characterize the inflammatory profile of hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Mureș County, Romania, at the point of admission and one month post-discharge.

pmc-12752269.title: An oral engineered cerium-peptide composite microsphere inhibits inflammatory bowel disease and reverses chronic fibrosis​​
pmc-12752269.creator: Wenyu Qiao, Luling Yang, Yu Liu, Huaiyuan Zhang, Zhihuan Zheng, Tianheng Gu, Jiaxi Zhu, Xinyi Hu, Gangze Li, Yuxia Zhang, Meng Xiao, Lin Zhang
pmc-12752269.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and dysbiosis of the gut microbiota are pivotal contributors to the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and associated fibrosis. In this study, a microfluidic approach was utilized to fabricate a multifunctional therapeutic microsphere system by encapsulating hollow mesoporous cerium oxide nanoparticles (HCeO2) loaded with KP1 short peptides-specific inhibitors of the TGF-β/Smad signaling pathway. The resulting composite formulation (KP1@HCeO₂@SAM) was designed to achieve synergistic antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antifibrotic effects.

pmc-13541095.title: Digital Health Engagement Behaviors in US Family Caregivers: Trend Analysis Using the Health Information National Trends Survey 2019-2022 Data
pmc-13541095.creator: Lena Lee, Elisa Son, Li Yang, Chantal Gerrard, Jenny Yarmovsky, Gwenyth Wallen
pmc-13541095.description: BackgroundDigital health has provided caregivers with access to supportive resources without space-time restrictions. Caregivers’ digital health engagement behaviors can help them track their own health and that of care recipients as well as communicate with others. While digital health tools have become more prevalent since the COVID-19 pandemic, the trend in caregiver engagement has been less explored.

pmc-13606910.title: Prescribed Rest Intervals in Home-Based Exercise Therapy and Rehabilitation: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework for Temporal Fidelity
pmc-13606910.creator: Nouf H. Alkhamees, Marilyn Gilyana, Sameer Badri Al-Mhanna, Alexios Batrakoulis
pmc-13606910.description: Adherence to home-based exercise programs is central to rehabilitation, yet adherence to prescribed rest intervals remains largely unexplored. This narrative review synthesized relevant literature identified through targeted, purposive searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for publications from 2000 to 20 July 2026, supplemented by reference-list screening.
